title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Let K be an abstract topological field that is isomorphic to C, with no isomorphism chosen. Let X be an algebraic K-scheme.

(1) X_top. The space X(K), with the topology induced from K, is defined intrinsically, so the Betti cohomology H^*(X_top, K) is defined. If X is smooth, the algebraic de Rham cohomology H^*(X) = H^*(X, Omega^._X) is defined together with its Hodge filtration. Grothendieck calls this 'cohomologie de Hodge'. It does not depend on the topology of K.

(2) Comparison. A topological isomorphism u : K -> C turns X into a complex variety X_u. Grothendieck's algebraic de Rham theorem (GAGA plus the holomorphic Poincare lemma) then gives an isomorphism H^*(X_top, K) ≅ H^*(X).
- There are exactly two choices of u, namely u and c∘u, where c is complex conjugation.
- The claim is that the comparison does not depend on u. Equivalently, for K = C the comparison maps for X and for X^c = X ⊗_{C,c} C differ only by applying c to the coefficients of H^*(X_top, C). This holds because the analytic structure of X^c is the conjugate of that of X, and integrals of conjugate forms are conjugates of integrals.
- So the de Rham–Betti comparison is canonical over any 'C-like' topological field.

(3) Real structure. There is a unique continuous embedding R -> K: it is the closure of Q in K. Hence H^*(X_top, R) ⊂ H^*(X_top, K) ≅ H^*(X) is a canonical real structure on the K-vector space H^*(X). This holds even when X has no model over R.
- It yields a canonical semilinear conjugation on H^*(X).
- The margin, partly legible, seems to record the corresponding +/- pieces.

(4) Hodge decomposition. For X smooth projective, a choice of u gives the Hodge decomposition phi : ⊕_{p,q} H^q(X, Omega^p) ≅ H^*(X), compatible with the Hodge filtration. Since H^{p,q} = F^p ∩ conj(F^q), and both the filtration and the conjugation are u-independent, phi is canonical.

Purpose. This is a preparatory step, continued on the next page, toward attaching a canonical Hodge decomposition of de Rham cohomology to smooth projective varieties over:
- topological fields isomorphic to C;
- fields isomorphic to R, by Galois descent along K'/K with pi = Z/2;
- then over abstract fields, after choosing a locally compact non-discrete topology T on K.

The previous page studies motives over R, real Frobenius f_∞, the Weil operator C and maximal compacts in Mumford–Tate-type groups. So this page builds the Hodge-realization side of the 'motifs sur R' discussion: the Hodge realization of a motive over an abstract field equipped with an archimedean topology.
errors: 'isom. injectif continu' for R -> K should read 'homomorphisme (plongement) injectif continu'. It is unique because it is determined on Q and extends by continuity.

Conjugation is semilinear, so the '+' and '-' pieces of H^*(X) suggested in the margin are real subspaces (H_R and i·H_R), not K-subspaces. The intended statement is presumably the real decomposition. The fully worked version of this is the marginal note on the next page, where the -1 eigenspace of the pi action on X_C,top matters.

The next page extends the argument to 'corps top. loc. (quasi) compact non discret'. As written this would include p-adic fields, where no canonical Hodge decomposition of de Rham cohomology exists. Presumably only archimedean (connected) locally compact fields, i.e. R and C, are intended.

Independence of u holds for K- (or Q-) coefficients. It would fail for integral Tate-twisted structures such as Z(1) = 2πiZ, whose orientation depends on u. Grothendieck implicitly avoids this by using untwisted coefficients.

ideas.what: Betti–de Rham comparison over an abstract topological field isomorphic to C is independent of the chosen isomorphism with C (compatibility of the comparison with complex conjugation X -> X^c).
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of the de Rham comparison isomorphism with conjugation / transport of structure; independence of the embedding sigma for archimedean places up to conjugation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; used systematically by Deligne (Valeurs de fonctions L et périodes d'intégrales, 1979; Hodge cycles on abelian varieties, 1982)
ideas.where_published: The comparison itself is in Grothendieck, 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (Publ. IHES 29, 1966); the independence remark unsure

ideas.what: Canonical real structure H^*(X_top, R) ⊂ H^*(X) on de Rham cohomology of a smooth variety over a C-like topological field, even with no real model.
ideas.modern_name: Real structure / complex conjugation on de Rham cohomology via Betti comparison
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard Hodge theory; Deligne (F_∞ and real structures, 1979)

ideas.what: Canonical Hodge decomposition of H^*_dR(X) for X smooth projective over a topological field ≅ C (and, by Galois descent, ≅ R), independent of the identification with C.
ideas.modern_name: Hodge realization of motives over fields with an archimedean place; Hodge decomposition as H^{p,q} = F^p ∩ conj(F^q)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hodge/Deligne; formalized in Deligne–Milne–Ogus–Shih (1982) and Deligne's 1979 L-functions paper

deep.surprise_reason: The page carefully but routinely checks that the de Rham comparison, the real structure and the Hodge decomposition are canonical over an abstract topological field ≅ C. This is standard (implicit in Deligne's work on F_∞ and absolute Hodge cycles). It is mildly interesting as evidence that Grothendieck was setting up Hodge realizations over abstract fields with a chosen archimedean topology around 1969–72, but it contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'Soit K un corps topologique isomorphe à C' — the image reads 'corps topologique(s)'; the meaning is unchanged.
'notant [?] i : R -> C un isom[?] injectif continu unique[?]' — the map is R -> K (unique continuous injective homomorphism); 'isom' is likely 'homom.' or 'plongement'.

The left-margin vertical text is largely illegible. It appears to say roughly 'sur R !) d'où une R-structure sur H^*(X), définie par H^*(X_top, R) ... H^*(X)^- ... H^*(X)^+'; the transcription's guesses here should be treated as uncertain.
The insertion 'si X est non sing.' (or 'non singulier') is written above the line before 'la cohomologie de Hodge est définie'. It is correctly placed in the transcription.
